cohort: The study included 482 full-term newborns (>38 weeks' gestation and birth weight >2500 g) with no abnormalities, with data extracted from electronic health records before and after a guideline change regarding hat use.
finding: The use of hats on infants at birth had no statistically significant impact on newborn thermoregulation or the incidence of hypothermia within 24 hours of birth.
